sections.title: Notebook history and charts
sections.what: Checks the call history table and its filter, the three charts with their text descriptions, the small-sample warnings, optional evidence screenshots, and that signed-out visitors are sent to sign in.
sections.why: Covers the full notebook view a user sees after making calls, including the honesty warnings.
sections.watch_out: The screenshot setting writes files into the evidence folder, so it should only be on when collecting evidence.

summary: Browser test of the personal Notebook: call history with filters, a reliability diagram, a Brier score chart, a skill radar, and small-sample warnings.
purpose: Confirms a user's record of calls is shown with the right charts and honest warnings about small samples.
why: Users judge their own skill from these charts, so they must render correctly and warn when a sample is too small to mean much.
how: It creates a user, confirms the notebook is empty, locks three calls using fixture moments, and reloads. It checks the history table has three rows and shows point changes. It checks each chart is present with a description and the expected points. It checks small-sample warnings are shown. When the EVIDENCE environment setting is on, it saves desktop and mobile screenshots. It then filters by chase tempo, expects one row and a one-call warning, and runs an accessibility check. A separate test checks the notebook asks signed-out visitors to sign in.
inputs: A new user, fixture moments, and the notebook page.
outputs: Pass or fail for history, charts, warnings and filtering, plus optional screenshots.
risks: Screenshot saving writes files into the docs evidence folder when the setting is on. Counts and warning wording are fixed.
debug: If charts are missing, check that the chart descriptions match the expected wording. If the filter fails, check the link and the URL parameter.
